observations: A wide, roughly rectangular head with two pointed peaks at the top is outlined in heavy black lines against a pale background covered in gray washes and loose black spike marks; four framed rectangular panels fill the face area.

Each panel holds a distinct layered pattern: upper-left has blue and red looping lines around a teal oval; upper-right holds a red rectangle with yellow zigzag border; lower-left shows red crossed diagonals over a pink grid with a small triangle; lower-right frames a single red-circled form with concentric yellow and blue loops.
A purple zigzag line runs horizontally across the lower face, and a short red horizontal stroke extends from the right side of the head into the background.
reading: Four framed panels replace expected facial features, each running its own small system of loops, crosses, and zigzags in red, blue, yellow, and teal. The result reads less as a face and more as a display board — something to be scanned rather than met. The purple zigzag at the mouth edge and the single circled form in the lower-right panel introduce an asymmetry that pulls against the otherwise grid-like arrangement.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbors #244 and #246 share the pointed-ear head form but differ sharply: #244 fills its ground with saturated cobalt blue and uses white-ringed circular eyes; #246 shifts to a black figure against a fragmented color field. #245 sits between them with a pale ground and panel-divided face.

connections.reason: Both share the pointed-ear head silhouette and yellow zigzag line patterns, but #244 uses a saturated blue ground with white circular eyes while #245 uses a pale ground and replaces the eyes with layered rectangular panels.

In #1, large goggle-like frames over the eye area are packed with layered colored loops and marks, offering a close formal parallel to the panel-within-face structure in #245, though #1 uses a dark ground and denser line layering.

lookingQuestion: The four panels each contain a different internal pattern — what do you notice about how the lines inside each panel relate to or ignore the lines in the panels next to it?
ambiguities: The lower-left panel contains crossed diagonals and a small triangle shape that could be read as a symbol or as pure mark-making; no supplied evidence resolves this.
The red horizontal stroke extending from the right side of the head is visible but its relationship to the rest of the composition is unclear from the image alone.
